questions.question: The cost of 5 chairs and 3 tables is ₹12,500, while the cost of 3 chairs and 5 tables is ₹15,500. Find the cost of 2 chairs and 2 tables.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum both equations to find the cost of **8 chairs and 8 tables**.

(5C + 3T) + (3C + 5T) = 12,500 + 15,500 ⇒ **8C + 8T = ₹28,000**.

To find the cost of **2 chairs and 2 tables**, divide the total sum by 4.

Cost = 28,000 ÷ 4 = 7,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of **5 chairs** and **3 tables** = ₹12,500

Cost of **3 chairs** and **5 tables** = ₹15,500

**Formula Used:**

Total Cost = (Cost per unit × Quantity)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3149df27356b6f8b4b63b4c5a5a94bde04d36b457fdbb25bf3f4ba2e94dce7ff.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the cost of one **chair** be C and one **table** be T.

⇒ 5C + 3T = 12,500 — (Equation 1)

⇒ 3C + 5T = 15,500 — (Equation 2)

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (5C + 3C) + (3T + 5T) = 12,500 + 15,500

⇒ 8C + 8T = 28,000

⇒ 8 × (C + T) = 28,000

⇒ C + T = 28,000 ÷ 8

⇒ C + T = 3,500

We need the cost of **2 chairs and 2 tables**:

⇒ 2 × (C + T) = 2 × 3,500

⇒ 2C + 2T = 7,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,000.**

questions.question: Three positive numbers are in proportion such that the ratio of the first number to the second number is the same as the ratio of the second number to the third number. If the first number is 16 and the second number is 24, find the value of the third number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The numbers are in **continued proportion**, so the ratio 16 : 24 must equal the ratio 24 : third number.

Simplify the first ratio: 16 : 24 = 2 : 3.

This means the second ratio must also be 2 : 3.

If 2 units = 24, then 1 unit = 12.

Therefore, 3 units = 12 × 3 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number = 16, Second number = 24.

**Formula Used:** For three numbers a, b, and c in **continued proportion**, a ÷ b = b ÷ c.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b777991df15fb14bebcb40c3309b5440d3dadf1bbe1fd3085ad43cf4f60b5ea5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **third number** be c.

⇒ 16 ÷ 24 = 24 ÷ c

⇒ (16 × c) = (24 × 24)

⇒ 16c = 576

⇒ c = 576 ÷ 16

⇒ c = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion, then b is called the **mean proportional** between a and c, where b = √(a × c).

Third Proportional

In the proportion a : b = b : c, the value c is known as the **third proportional** to a and b, calculated as c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For four numbers a, b, c, and d in proportion (a : b = c : d), d is the **fourth proportional**, where d = (b × c) ÷ a.

**New Scenario:**

 **New Cost Price (CP₂)**
 100x − 25% of 100x = 75x

 **New Selling Price (SP₂)**
 115x − 294

In this new scenario, the **Profit** made is **30%**.

We can express the **New Selling Price** in terms of the **New Cost Price** and **Profit**:

SP₂ = CP₂ + 30% of CP₂

SP₂ = 75x + (30/100) × 75x

SP₂ = 75x + 22.5x = 97.5x

**Equating the New Selling Price values:**

Now, we equate the two different expressions for **SP₂** to find the value of x:

115x − 294 = 97.5x

115x − 97.5x = 294

17.5x = 294

x = 294 / 17.5

x = 16.8

**Calculating the Original Cost Price:**

CP₁ = 100 × 16.8 = 1,680

The **cost price** of the article is **₹1,680**.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following schemes on toys of the same marked price.

(A) Successive discounts of 24% and 33% on any number of toys bought.

(B) Successive discounts of 39%, 37% and 23% on any number of toys bought.

(C) 24% discount on the first 2 toys and 12% discount on each toy thereon.

(D) 2 toys free of cost on buying 5 toys.

A customer wants to buy 5 toys. Which of the above schemes is the least beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the **Effective Discount** for 5 toys in each scheme:

Scheme A: 24 + 33 − (24 × 33 ÷ 100) = 49.08%

Scheme B: Successive 39%, 37%, 23% → Obviously higher than 50% (approx 70.4%)

Scheme C: (2 × 24% + 3 × 12%) ÷ 5 = (48 + 36) ÷ 5 = 16.8%

Scheme D: 2 ÷ (5 + 2) × 100 ≈ 28.57%

Comparing all, 16.8% is the **minimum discount**.

**∴ The correct answer is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Assume the **Marked Price (MP)** of each toy = ₹100. For 5 toys, total MP = ₹500.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ae6983642701a8d6c17d6161c22df9ee911d81318747989f61b2a5bc70320df.png] 

**Scheme A (Successive 24% and 33%):**

⇒ Net Discount % = 24 + 33 − (24 × 33)/100 = 57 − 7.92 = 49.08%

**Scheme B (Successive 39%, 37% and 23%):**

⇒ After 39% and 37%: 39 + 37 − (39 × 37)/100 = 76 − 14.43 = 61.57%

⇒ Net Discount % = 61.57 + 23 − (61.57 × 23)/100 = 84.57 − 14.16 = 70.41%

**Scheme C (24% on first 2, 12% on rest):**

⇒ Total Discount = (2 × 24) + (3 × 12) = 48 + 36 = ₹84

⇒ Effective Discount % = (84 ÷ 500) × 100 = 16.8%

**Scheme D (2 toys free on 5 toys bought):**

⇒ Total items = 5 + 2 = 7 toys

⇒ Discount % = (Free items ÷ Total items) × 100 = (2 ÷ 7) × 100 ≈ 28.57%

The **Least Beneficial** scheme for the customer is the one with the **minimum discount**.

**∴ The correct answer is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

Buy X Get Y Free

The effective discount percentage for such schemes is calculated as [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

Customer vs Shopkeeper Benefit

A customer seeks the maximum discount (Most Beneficial), while the shopkeeper seeks the minimum discount (Least Beneficial to customer).

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 32 and their product is 220. The positive difference between them is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct algebraic identity: **(Difference)² = (Sum)² − 4 × (Product)**

Given **Sum = 32** and **Product = 220**.

⇒ (Difference)² = 32² − 4 × 220

⇒ (Difference)² = 1024 − 880 = 144

⇒ **Difference** = √144 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the two **positive numbers** be x and y.

**Given:**

1. x + y = 32

2. x × y = 220

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ef6526ac02fccbae99db1ba66a63c23ce642c6135cba73e0cece938f10b49d2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x + y)² = 32²

⇒ x² + y² + 2xy = 1024

⇒ x² + y² + 2(220) = 1024

⇒ x² + y² = 1024 − 440 = 584

⇒ (x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy

⇒ (x − y)² = 584 − 440 = 144

⇒ x − y = √144 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Sum and Difference

The relation between sum, difference, and product is given by the identity: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Quadratic Equation Roots

If the sum (S) and product (P) of two numbers are known, the numbers are roots of the equation: t² − St + P = 0.

Finding Individual Values

Once the sum (S) and difference (D) are known, the larger number is (S + D) ÷ 2 and the smaller number is (S − D) ÷ 2.

Assume the **Mean** (40) as the balance point where the sum of deviations is zero.

**Given:** Mean (&bar;x) = 40. Data points (x) and frequencies (f) are mapped below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d61d56e63a5d0405b47fe861a4adac853e430417e634d002086f285404a7edf.png] 

**Formula:** Mean (&bar;x) = ∑fᵢxᵢ ÷ ∑fᵢ

⇒ ∑fᵢxᵢ = (10 × 2) + (20 × 3) + (30 × 1) + (40 × 4) + (50 × f) + (60 × 4)

⇒ ∑fᵢxᵢ = 20 + 60 + 30 + 160 + 50f + 240 = 510 + 50f

⇒ ∑fᵢ = 2 + 3 + 1 + 4 + f + 4 = 14 + f

⇒ 40(14 + f) = 510 + 50f

⇒ 560 + 40f = 510 + 50f

⇒ 560 − 510 = 50f − 40f

⇒ 50 = 10f ⇒ f = 5

Arithmetic Mean of Discrete Series

Calculated as the sum of products of observations and their frequencies divided by the total frequency: &bar;x = ∑fx / ∑f.

The algebraic sum of deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero, i.e., ∑fᵢ(xᵢ − &bar;x) = 0.

A shortcut formula where Mean = A + (∑fd / ∑f), where A is the assumed mean and d = x − A is the deviation.

questions.question: Sixteen identical solid cubes, each of side 2 cm, are melted and recast into a cuboid whose length is twice its breadth and height equals its breadth. Find the volume of the cuboid.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total volume remains **constant** when objects are melted and recast.

Volume of **16 identical cubes** = 16 × (Side)³

Volume = 16 × (2 cm)³ = 16 × 8 cm³ = 128 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 128 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Sixteen identical cubes** with side = 2 cm. For the cuboid, **length (L)** = 2 × **breadth (B)** and **height (H)** = **breadth (B)**.

**Formula Used:** Volume of cube = a³ | Volume of cuboid = L × B × H

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61aa24eadf0d348933d9041cc77d1ed1c4331e10ea09fc71f10ad5e97aa475c1.png] 

⇒ Volume of one solid cube = (2 cm)³ = 8 cm³

⇒ Total volume of 16 cubes = 16 × 8 cm³ = 128 cm³

⇒ Let the breadth of the cuboid be **B**.

⇒ Length **L = 2B** and Height **H = B**.

⇒ Volume of cuboid = L × B × H = (2B) × B × B = 2B³

⇒ Since volume is conserved: 2B³ = 128

⇒ B³ = 64 ⇒ B = 4 cm

⇒ Volume of cuboid = 2 × (4)³ = 2 × 64 = 128 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 128 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation Principle

When a physical object is **melted and recast** into one or more different shapes, the **total volume** remains unchanged, assuming no material is lost in the process.

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area (TSA) of a cuboid is given by the formula: 2 × (LB + BH + HL). For the calculated dimensions (8, 4, 4), TSA = 2 × (32 + 16 + 32) = 160 cm².

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The **space diagonal** (longest distance between opposite corners) is calculated as √(L² + B² + H²).

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution directs the State to protect and improve the environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 48A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 48A** of the **Indian Constitution** specifically mandates the **State** to endeavor to protect and improve the **environment** and to safeguard the **forests** and **wildlife** of the country.
 
• This provision was incorporated into the Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, which was passed during the internal emergency and is frequently called the **Mini-Constitution** due to the vast changes it introduced.
 
• It is situated within **Part IV** of the Constitution, which contains the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**; these serve as fundamental guidelines for the **Central** and **State governments** while formulating legislation and policies.
 
• While **Directive Principles** are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced directly by a court of law, **Article 37** declares that they are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the **State** to apply them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 39A**:

 
 
• Inserted by the **42nd Amendment Act**, it directs the State to ensure that the operation of the legal system promotes **justice** on a basis of **equal opportunity**.
 
• It specifically requires the State to provide **free legal aid** to ensure that justice is not denied to any citizen due to **economic** or other disabilities.
 
 
 
• **Article 43A**:
 
 
• This article was also added in **1976** and mandates the State to take steps to secure the **participation of workers** in the management of undertakings or **industrial establishments**.
 
• It reflects the **socialist principles** of the Indian Constitution by empowering the labor force within the industrial framework.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A(g)**:
 
 
• While Article 48A is a duty of the State, **Article 51A(g)** establishes a **Fundamental Duty** for every **citizen of India** to protect and improve the natural environment including **lakes, rivers, and wildlife**.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the Konkan Coast along its western shoreline?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Konkan Coast** is a **720-kilometer** long rugged section of the western coastline of the **Indian Peninsula**, stretching from **Daman** in the north to **Goa** in the south.
 
• In the state of **Maharashtra**, the coast covers several key districts, including **Mumbai City**, **Mumbai Suburban**, **Thane**, **Palghar**, **Raigad**, **Ratnagiri**, and **Sindhudurg**.
 
• Geographically, it is positioned between the **Western Ghats** (also known as the **Sahyadri** mountain range) to the east and the **Arabian Sea** to the west.
 
• The region is characterized by **laterite soil** and receives high annual rainfall from the **Southwest Monsoon**, making it suitable for the cultivation of **Alphonso mangoes**, **cashews**, **coconuts**, and **betel nuts**.
 
• Historically, the **Konkan** region has been a vital maritime gateway, featuring prominent ports and coastal forts like **Janjira**, **Sindhudurg**, and **Raigad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odisha**:

 
 
• The coastline of this eastern state is known as the **Utkal Coast**.
 
• It is home to the **Mahanadi River** delta and **Chilika Lake**, which is the largest brackish water lagoon in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**:
 
 
• The shoreline of this state is referred to as the **Kanara Coast** or **Karavali**.

questions.question: You can often hear a person speaking from behind a tall fence even if you cannot see them. Which property of sound waves explains this phenomenon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diffraction** refers to the physical phenomenon where a wave encounters an obstacle or an opening and **bends around the corners** or spreads out as it passes through.
 
• This property is common to all types of waves, including **sound, light, and water waves**, but its visibility depends heavily on the ratio of the **wavelength** to the size of the obstacle.
 
• The **audible frequency range** for humans (20 Hz to 20,000 Hz) corresponds to **wavelengths** approximately between **1.7 centimeters and 17 meters** in air.
 
• Because these wavelengths are comparable to the dimensions of everyday objects like **fences, buildings, and doorways**, sound waves easily bend over or around these barriers into the **geometrical shadow** region.
 
• In the given scenario, while the **rectilinear propagation of light** (due to its extremely small wavelength of about 400 to 700 nanometers) prevents us from seeing the person, the **long wavelengths of sound** allow the waves to diffract over the **tall fence** and reach the listener.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polarization**

 
 
• It is the process by which the vibrations of a **transverse wave** (like light) are restricted to a single plane of direction.
 
• Sound waves in air are **longitudinal waves** (vibrations are parallel to the direction of travel) and therefore **cannot be polarized**.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• This involves the **change in direction** of a wave as it passes from one medium to another with a **different density** or speed, such as sound traveling through air layers of **different temperatures**.
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• This is the **bouncing back** of a wave when it strikes a boundary or a hard surface. Common examples in sound include **echoes and reverberations**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding organic farming?

options.text: Organic farming is beneficial for soil biota.

• **Organic farming** is a holistic production management system that promotes and enhances **agro-ecosystem health**, including **biodiversity** and **biological cycles**, making it inherently **environment-friendly**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It prioritizes **soil health** by utilizing **organic manures**, **green manure**, and **compost**, which nourish **soil biota** such as **earthworms** and **beneficial microbes**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• A fundamental principle of this agricultural practice is the exclusion of **synthetic chemicals**, including **chemical fertilizers**, **synthetic pesticides**, and **genetically modified organisms (GMOs)**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Unlike modern industrial agriculture that relies on **capital-intensive high technology** and **precision engineering**, organic farming is **knowledge-intensive** and relies on **ecological processes** and **traditional practices** adapted to local conditions. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

• **Crop Rotation:** Growing different crops in sequence to maintain **soil productivity** and break **pest cycles**.
 
• **Biological Pest Control:** Using **predatory insects** and **bio-pesticides** like **Neem** or **Panchagavya** instead of toxic sprays.
 
• **Bio-fertilizers:** Utilizing **Rhizobium**, **Azotobacter**, and **Blue-Green Algae** to fix atmospheric nitrogen.
 
 
 
• **Indian Context:**
 
 
• **Sikkim** became the world s first **fully organic state** in **2016**, demonstrating the viability of chemical-free farming.

• Certification is managed by the **National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP)** under **APEDA** and the **Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India)**.

questions.question: Which Acts are being amended to allow private sector participation in India’s nuclear energy sector?

options.text: Atomic Energy Act, 1962 & Energy Conservation Act, 2001

__
 
• The **Atomic Energy Act, 1962** is the primary legislative framework that governs the development, control, and use of atomic energy in India. Currently, **Section 3** of this Act restricts the design, construction, and operation of nuclear power plants to the **Central Government** or a **Government Company** where the state holds at least 51 percent equity. Proposed amendments aim to allow **private sector** entities to participate, especially in the deployment of **Small Modular Reactors (SMRs)**.
 
• The **Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage (CLND) Act, 2010** provides for civil liability for nuclear damage and prompt compensation to victims of a nuclear incident. It has been a significant barrier for private participation due to **Section 17** (Right of Recourse) and **Section 46**, which create ambiguity regarding the liability of **suppliers** and operators. Amending this framework is considered vital to providing the **legal certainty** required for private investments and **insurance** coverage in the nuclear power sector.
 
• India targets a significant increase in its nuclear capacity to reach its **Net Zero** goals by **2070**. By amending these two specific acts, the government intends to transition from a purely **state-led model** to a collaborative model that includes **private equity** and technical expertise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• This Act governs the **generation, transmission, and distribution** of electricity in India but does not override the specific restrictions placed on nuclear energy by the **Atomic Energy Act**.
 
• It was enacted to promote competition and **delicense thermal generation**, yet nuclear power remains a **reserved sector** under the 1962 legislation.
 
 
 
• **Energy Conservation Act, 2001**:
 
 
• This Act focuses on **energy efficiency** and conservation measures through the establishment of the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)**.
 
• It does not regulate the **ownership or operational rights** of nuclear power facilities, making it irrelevant to the structural shift toward private nuclear participation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural runoff**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-point source (NPS) pollution** refers to contamination that does not originate from a single, discrete location or a specific pipe. Instead, it results from **diffuse sources** across a wide geographic area.
 
• **Agricultural runoff** is the leading cause of NPS pollution globally. When it rains or snow melts, the water washes over farmland, picking up **synthetic fertilizers**, **herbicides**, **insecticides**, and animal waste containing **bacteria** and **nutrients** like **nitrogen** and **phosphorus**.
 
• Because these pollutants are spread across thousands of acres and enter water bodies through broad overland flow rather than a concentrated channel, they are nearly impossible to trace to a single culprit.
 
• The **Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)** and frameworks like the **Clean Water Act** classify this as NPS because it is driven by **precipitation** and land management practices rather than end-of-pipe industrial processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• This category includes any **identifiable source** where pollutants are discharged from a specific point, such as a pipe or a ditch.
 
• **Industrial discharge pipe**: These are regulated under **permit systems** because the exact volume and chemical composition of the waste exiting the factory can be monitored at the exit point.
 
• **Sewage outlet**: Municipal **wastewater treatment plants** discharge treated or untreated sewage through discrete pipes into rivers or oceans, making them **stationary point sources**.
 
• **Urban stormwater drain**: Although the source of the water is city-wide runoff, the **Municipal Separate Storm Sewer Systems (MS4s)** collect this water into a network of pipes and discharge it at specific outfalls, thus they are treated as **point sources** in regulatory contexts.

questions.question: Which substance would you use to test if lemon juice contains acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Litmus paper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Litmus paper** is a specialized **acid-base indicator** produced by treating filter paper with natural water-soluble dyes extracted from **lichens**, primarily **Roccella tinctoria**.
 
• **Lemon juice** contains a high concentration of **citric acid** (C₆H₈O₇), which is an organic acid responsible for the fruit's low **pH level**, typically measured between **2.0 and 3.0**.
 
• When **blue litmus paper** is exposed to the **hydrogen ions (H⁺)** present in lemon juice, a chemical reaction occurs that changes the pigment's structure, turning the paper **red**.
 
• This color transition from **blue to red** is the standard qualitative test used in chemistry to confirm the presence of an **acidic substance**.
 
• Unlike other substances, **litmus paper** does not significantly react with or alter the chemical composition of the sample, making it a reliable tool for **pH identification** in laboratory and educational settings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baking soda** (Sodium Bicarbonate):

 
 
• It is a **chemical compound** with the formula **NaHCO₃** and acts as a **weak base**.
 
• While it reacts with acids to produce **carbon dioxide** (CO₂) gas and **effervescence**, it is primarily a reactant rather than a standard **color-changing indicator**.
 
 
 
• **Sugar** (Sucrose):
 
 
• **Sucrose** (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) is a **neutral organic compound** that does not dissociate into ions that would change the **pH** of a solution.
 
• It does not exhibit any **chromogenic properties** when mixed with acids, making it useless for detection.
 
 
 
• **Water**:
 
 
• Pure water is **chemically neutral** with a **pH of 7.0** and serves as the **universal solvent**.
 
• It does not provide any visual or chemical signal to distinguish between **acidic**, **basic**, or **neutral** solutions on its own.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale**:
 
 
• Developed by **S.P.L. Sorensen**, the scale measures the **logarithmic concentration** of hydrogen ions.
 
• Values **below 7** represent **acidity**, while values **above 7** represent **alkalinity**.

questions.question: Which language is known for its unique script called "Gurmukhi"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjabi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Punjabi** is an Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly in the **Punjab** region of **India** and **Pakistan**. In India, it is one of the **22 scheduled languages** mentioned in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** and is written using the **Gurmukhi script**.
 
• The term **Gurmukhi** literally means **from the mouth of the Guru**. It was standardized and popularized by **Guru Angad Dev Ji**, the second **Sikh Guru**, during the **16th century** to record the hymns and teachings of the Gurus.
 
• The script was specifically designed to be easy for the common people to learn, thereby breaking the monopoly of the priestly classes over religious texts. The **Guru Granth Sahib**, the holy scripture of **Sikhism**, is written entirely in this script.
 
• Structurally, Gurmukhi is an **abugida**, where each consonant has an inherent vowel that can be modified with vowel signs. It contains **35 primary letters**, often referred to as **Panti Akhar**, and is written from left to right.
 
• Historically, Gurmukhi evolved from the **Landa** script and belongs to the **Sharada** family of scripts, which were prevalent in **North-Western India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Scripts and Languages**:

 
 
• **Bengali**: This language uses the **Bengali-Assamese script**, which is the fifth most widely used writing system in the world. It evolved from the **Brahmic** family and is the official script for **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• **Hindi**: It is written in the **Devanagari script**, which is shared by other languages like **Sanskrit**, **Marathi**, and **Nepali**. It is distinguished by the **Shirorekha** (horizontal line) running along the top of the letters.
 
• **Urdu**: This language typically utilizes the **Nastaliq** style of the **Perso-Arabic script**. Unlike Gurmukhi or Devanagari, Urdu is written from **right to left** and is known for its cursive, calligraphic nature.

questions.question: Article 371A of the Constitution of India states 'privilege of special status was also accorded to the North-Eastern State of Nagaland'. This represents which federalism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asymmetric federalism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asymmetric federalism** refers to a federal system where different constituent states or units within a federation possess unequal powers or specific constitutional protections based on their unique historical, cultural, or geographical circumstances.
 
• **Article 371A** was inserted into the **Constitution of India** by the **13th Amendment Act, 1962**, following an agreement between the **Government of India** and the **Naga Peoples Convention** in 1960.
 
• Under this provision, **Acts of Parliament** regarding **Naga religious or social practices**, **Naga customary law**, and **ownership and transfer of land** do not apply to **Nagaland** unless the **State Legislative Assembly** passes a resolution to that effect.
 
• By granting **Nagaland** a level of autonomy and special status not shared by other states like **Uttar Pradesh** or **Kerala**, the Indian Constitution demonstrates a **flexible federal structure** designed to manage diversity and ethnic aspirations.
 
• This differential treatment of sub-national units is the hallmark of **asymmetric federalism**, which is also reflected in other articles ranging from **371** to **371J** for various other states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centralised federalism**:

 
 
• Refers to a system where the **Union Government** holds overarching authority, often exemplified in India by **Article 248** (residuary powers) and **Article 356** (President’s Rule).
 
 
 
• **Competitive federalism**:
 
 
• A model where states compete for **investments** and **resources** to improve their economic standing, frequently promoted through indices like the **SDG India Index** by **NITI Aayog**.
 
 
 
• **Bargaining federalism**:
 
 
• A term coined by political scientist **W.H. Morris-Jones** to describe the Indian context where the **Center** and **States** negotiate and haggle over political and financial concessions, especially during **coalition politics**.

questions.question: In India, the concept of judicial activism, as reflected through innovative interpretations of the Constitution and expansion of the scope of judicial review, was introduced during which of the following periods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mid-1970s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Judicial activism in India was introduced in the **mid-1970s** as a response to the institutional crisis faced by the judiciary during the **Internal Emergency** (1975−1977).
 
• It was pioneered by visionary judges, most notably **Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer** and **Justice P.N. Bhagwati**, who sought to make the legal system accessible to the poor and marginalized sections of society.
 
• The concept involves a proactive role played by the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** in protecting the **Fundamental Rights** of citizens and ensuring that the executive and legislature remain within their constitutional limits.
 
• The landmark judgment in **Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India (1978)** served as a catalyst, where the court expanded the scope of **Article 21** (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) to include the right to live with human dignity.
 
• During this period, the judiciary shifted from the traditional doctrine of **Locus Standi**, allowing any public-spirited individual to approach the court on behalf of those unable to do so, thus birthing **Public Interest Litigation (PIL)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Interest Litigation (PIL):**

 
 
• It is also known as **Social Action Litigation (SAL)**, a term coined by **Upendra Baxi**.
 
• The first major case was **Hussainara Khatoon vs. Home Secretary, State of Bihar** (1979), which led to the release of thousands of undertrial prisoners.
 
• It emphasizes justice over technicalities, often initiated through simple letters or telegrams addressed to the **Chief Justice of India**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Basis:**
 
 
• Judicial activism is rooted in the power of **Judicial Review** granted under **Article 13**, **Article 32** (Supreme Court), and **Article 226** (High Courts).
 
• It allows the court to strike down laws or executive actions that violate the **Basic Structure Doctrine**, established in the **Kesavananda Bharati** case (1973).
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Activism has led to significant advancements in **Environmental Law** (the 'Green Bench'), **Human Rights**, and the protection of **bonded labor** and **child labor**.

questions.question: Who led the Portuguese expedition that first landed in Calicut, India, in 1498?

• **Vasco da Gama** was a celebrated **Portuguese explorer** who successfully led the first maritime expedition from **Europe** to **India**, establishing the **Carreira da Índia**.
 
• The expedition set sail from **Lisbon** on **July 8, 1497**, with a fleet of four ships, including the flagship **São Gabriel**.
 
• After navigating around the **Cape of Good Hope** at the southern tip of Africa, the fleet reached the port of **Calicut** (now **Kozhikode**) on the **Malabar Coast** on **May 20, 1498**.
 
• Upon arrival, he was received by the **Zamorin** (Samudiri), the Hindu ruler of Calicut, to negotiate trade rights for spices like **pepper** and **cinnamon**.
 
• This voyage was a turning point in world history as it opened an all-sea route to the **East**, allowing **Portugal** to bypass the **Ottoman Empire** and **Venetian** monopolies on the spice trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• He commanded the **second Portuguese expedition** to India in **1500**.
 
• During this voyage, he veered far into the Atlantic and became the first European to reach the coast of **Brazil**.
 
 
 
• **Alfonso de Albuquerque**:
 
 
• He served as the second **Governor of Portuguese India** from **1509 to 1515** and is considered the founder of the Portuguese imperial system in Asia.
 
• He famously conquered **Goa** in **1510**, making it the headquarters of the **Portuguese State of India**.
 
 
 
• **Bartholomew Diaz**:
 
 
• In **1488**, he became the first European navigator to round the **Cape of Good Hope**, which he originally named the **Cape of Storms**.
 
• His journey proved that the **Atlantic** and **Indian Oceans** were connected, paving the way for **Vasco da Gama**.

questions.question: Which of the following strategies is crucial for fostering infrastructure development in developing countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promotion of public-private partnerships**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)** are long-term contracts between a **private party** and a **government entity** for providing a public asset or service, in which the private party bears significant risk and management responsibility.
 
• Developing countries often face a massive **infrastructure funding gap**. **PPPs** bridge this gap by leveraging **private capital** to finance large-scale projects like highways, airports, and power plants without placing an immediate strain on the **national budget**.
 
• This strategy promotes **managerial efficiency** and **innovation**. Private firms often utilize advanced technology and lean management practices to complete projects faster and more cost-effectively than traditional public procurement.
 
• **Risk Allocation** is a core feature of **PPPs**. Risks related to construction, operations, and maintenance are transferred to the private sector, while the government handles **regulatory** and **political risks**.
 
• The **World Bank** and the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** advocate for **PPPs** as a vital mechanism for achieving **Sustainable Development Goal 9 (SDG 9)**, which focuses on building resilient infrastructure and fostering innovation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**:

 
 
• Restricting investment prevents the inflow of **foreign exchange** and global technical expertise, which are critical for high-tech infrastructure like **smart grids** and **telecommunications**.
 
 
 
• **Inclusive Infrastructure**:
 
 
• Focusing solely on **urban areas** creates regional imbalances. Developing nations require **rural infrastructure** to improve **agricultural supply chains** and reduce poverty.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Constraints**:
 
 
• Sole reliance on government funding can lead to high **fiscal deficits** and increased **sovereign debt**, especially in nations with a narrow **tax base**.
 
 
 
• **Models of PPP**:
 
 
• Common models include **Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT)**, **Build-Own-Operate (BOO)**, and **Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM)**, each offering different levels of private involvement and financial risk.

questions.question: Which of the following geographical factors most directly influences the location and growth of human settlements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Availability of fresh water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fresh water** is the most fundamental requirement for human survival, serving critical needs such as **drinking**, **cooking**, and **sanitation**.
 
• Historically, the **River Valley Civilizations**—including the **Indus Valley** (Indus River), **Mesopotamia** (Tigris and Euphrates), and **Ancient Egypt** (Nile)—emerged specifically because of the proximity to perennial water sources.
 
• Water is a primary driver for **agricultural productivity**; the growth of settlements depends on a steady food supply, which is only possible through **irrigation** and fertile floodplains provided by rivers.
 
• Rivers and lakes provide natural **transportation routes** and **trade links**, which were historically the most efficient ways to move goods and people before the advent of modern infrastructure.
 
• In the modern era, **industrialization** and **urbanization** remain heavily dependent on water for cooling, processing, and generating **hydroelectric power**.
 
• Settlements located near water bodies often benefit from a **moderate climate** due to the land and sea breeze effect, making the environment more hospitable for long-term habitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Distance from the equator:** While it determines **climatic zones** (tropical, temperate, polar), humans have successfully adapted to various latitudes as long as resources like water and food are accessible.
 
• **Soil Characteristics:** The **fertility** and **texture** of soil are more important for settlement growth than the **color of local soil**, which is an aesthetic or mineralogical trait rather than a survival necessity.
 
• **Topography:** The **shape of nearby hills** can influence local drainage and defense (e.g., hill forts), but **flat plains** with water access are generally preferred for the mass expansion of human settlements.

questions.question: In Harappan Civilization, at Dholavira, ________ was/were used to build massive fortifications.

__
 
• **Dholavira**, located on the **Khadir Bet** island in the **Kutch** district of **Gujarat**, is one of the most remarkable cities of the **Indus Valley Civilization** (IVC).
 
• Unlike the brick-dominated cities of the Indus plains like **Harappa** and **Mohenjo-Daro**, Dholavira is unique for its extensive use of **stone** in monumental architecture and fortifications.
 
• The city featured a sophisticated **tripartite layout** consisting of a **Citadel**, a **Middle Town**, and a **Lower Town**, all of which were protected by massive **stone-faced** fortification walls.
 
• The fortifications were constructed using a combination of **sun-dried mud bricks** and **rubble stone**, often reinforced with **dressed stone** veneers to provide structural strength and aesthetic finish.
 
• The availability of local **sandstone** and **limestone** in the Rann of Kutch region allowed the Harappans at Dholavira to innovate with masonry techniques that were rare in other parts of the civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Distinctive Architectural Features**

 
 
• **Water Management**: Dholavira is world-renowned for its **water harvesting system**, which included 16 massive **rock-cut reservoirs** designed to store rainwater in an arid environment.
 
• **The Signboard**: Archaeologists discovered a large inscription at the northern gate of the citadel, often called the **Dholavira Signboard**, containing ten large-sized signs of the **Harappan script**.
 
• **UNESCO Status**: Due to its unique urban planning and hydraulic engineering, Dholavira was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **July 2021**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Materials**
 
 
• **Bricks**: While **burnt bricks** were the standard building material in the Indus river valley, Dholavira used them primarily for internal structures rather than the main facade of massive fortifications.
 
• **Wood**: This was used for roofs, doors, and columns but lacked the durability required for **massive fortifications**.
 
• **Granite**: Although stone was prevalent, the specific types used were primarily sedimentary stones like **sandstone** rather than granite.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is primarily responsible for the formation of badland topography in India?

The correct answer is __**Chambal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chambal River** is primarily responsible for the formation of **badland topography** in India, a unique landform characterized by a highly dissected and eroded landscape.
 
• This topography is created through a process known as **gully erosion**, where surface runoff carves deep channels into the soft alluvial soil of the **Chambal Valley**.
 
• The resulting landforms are locally known as the **Chambal Ravines** or **Bihad**, spanning across the states of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Rajasthan**, and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The intense erosion has rendered large tracts of land **unfit for cultivation**, leading to a landscape of sharp ridges, steep slopes, and narrow valleys that hinder **agricultural development**.
 
• The **semi-arid climate** of the region combined with the loose nature of the soil accelerates the rate of erosion during the **monsoon season**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chambal River**:

 
 
• It originates from the **Janapav Hills** of the **Vindhya Range** near Mhow in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It is a major **tributary** of the **Yamuna River** and is considered one of the cleanest rivers in India.
 
• The river basin supports critical wildlife, including the **Gharial**, **Red-crowned roof turtle**, and **Gangetic Dolphins**.
 
 
 
• **Gully Erosion vs. Sheet Erosion**:
 
 
• **Sheet erosion** involves the uniform removal of topsoil by water, whereas **gully erosion** creates deep, permanent channels that cannot be removed by normal tillage.
 
 
 
• **Other Rivers**:
 
 
• The **Ganga** and **Brahmaputra** are largely associated with **aggradational landforms** such as massive **floodplains** and the **Sundarbans Delta**.
 
• While the **Yamuna** experiences erosion, the classic **badland morphology** is a specific geographic feature defined by the **Chambal basin**.

questions.question: The Pallava temples at Mahabalipuram are made mainly from:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Granite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pallava temples** at **Mahabalipuram** (also known as **Mamallapuram**), dating back to the **7th and 8th centuries CE**, are distinguished by their use of local, hard-bound **granite** rather than the softer stones common in northern regions.
 
• The architecture at this site is categorized into three stages: **rock-cut cave temples**, **monolithic shrines** (known as **Rathas**), and **structural temples** built with blocks.
 
• The **Pancha Rathas** (Five Rathas), which are monolithic structures carved from a single outcropping of **pinkish-grey granite**, demonstrate the mastery of **Pallava** artisans over extremely hard stone during the reign of **Narasimhavarman I**.
 
• The **Shore Temple**, a designated **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, was constructed during the reign of **Narasimhavarman II** (Rajasimha) using dressed **granite** blocks to withstand the corrosive sea environment of the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The massive open-air relief known as the **Descent of the Ganges** or **Arjuna’s Penance** is meticulously carved onto two giant **granite** boulders, showcasing the transition of **Indian sculpture** towards the **Dravidian style**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alternative Construction Materials**

 
 
• **Sandstone**: While **granite** was the primary choice at **Mahabalipuram**, the **Pallava Dynasty** shifted to using **sandstone** for structural temples in their capital city of **Kanchipuram**, as seen in the **Kailasanathar Temple**.
 
• **Marble**: This material was rarely used in early **South Indian** architecture; it became prominent much later in **North Indian** sites like the **Dilwara Temples** and during the **Mughal Empire**.

questions.question: When moving down a group in the Modern Periodic Table, what happens to the number of valence electrons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Remains the same**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Modern Periodic Table** is organized into 18 vertical columns known as **Groups** and 7 horizontal rows known as **Periods**, arranged by increasing **Atomic Number**.
 
• Elements belonging to the same **Group** share similar chemical properties because they possess the same number of **valence electrons** in their **outermost shell**.
 
• As you move down a group, the **Principal Quantum Number** increases, meaning a new **electron shell** is added for each successive element.
 
• Despite the addition of shells, the number of electrons in the **highest energy level** remains constant; for example, all elements in **Group 1** (Alkali Metals) have exactly **one valence electron**.
 
• In **Group 17** (Halogens), elements like **Fluorine** and **Chlorine** both have **seven valence electrons**, which dictates their high reactivity and similar bonding behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Radius**

 
 
• The **atomic size** increases down a group because the addition of new **energy levels** increases the distance between the **nucleus** and the valence shell.
 
 
 
• **Metallic Character**
 
 
• This increases down a group as the **nuclear pull** on the valence electrons weakens, making it easier for the atom to lose electrons and form **positive ions**.
 
 
 
• **Electronegativity**
 
 
• This property typically decreases down a group because the increased **atomic radius** and **electron shielding** reduce the ability of the nucleus to attract a shared pair of electrons.
 
 
 
• **Valency**
 
 
• The **valency** of elements remains constant down a group since it depends directly on the number of **valence electrons** available for chemical bonding.

questions.question: A user wants to quickly pause work and resume in few minutes without waiting for the computer to reboot. The best option is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sleep mode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sleep mode** is a power-saving state that allows a computer to quickly resume full-power operation, usually within **several seconds**, when the user wants to start working again.
 
• In this state, the computer enters a low-power mode where the **operating system** saves the current state of all open applications, files, and settings into the **Random Access Memory (RAM)**.
 
• Because the data is stored in the **volatile memory (RAM)**, the system continues to draw a small amount of electricity to maintain the data integrity; if power is cut completely, unsaved data in the **RAM** is lost.
 
• This functionality is specifically designed for short breaks, such as a **few minutes** or an hour, effectively eliminating the need for a **cold boot** or **reboot sequence**, which requires loading the **Kernel** and **system drivers** from the slower secondary storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Complete Shutdown**:

 
 
• This process closes all software programs, clears the **RAM**, and terminates power to almost all hardware components.
 
• Resuming work requires a full **Power-On Self-Test (POST)** and **BIOS/UEFI** initialization, making it the slowest method to return to a workspace.
 
 
 
• **Reinstall OS**:
 
 
• This is a major maintenance procedure where the **Operating System** (such as **Windows** or **Linux**) is re-written to the storage drive.
 
• It is used to resolve **registry errors** or **malware** issues and would result in the loss of current unsaved work progress.
 
 
 
• **Format Disk**:
 
 
• This operation prepares a **Hard Disk Drive (HDD)** or **Solid State Drive (SSD)** for data storage by creating a new **file system** (like **NTFS** or **APFS**).
 
• It is a destructive process that erases all existing data on the partition, making it irrelevant for pausing a work session.

Some leaves are trees.

All chairs are trees.

(II) All trees are chairs.
